strings.CLL_Shoulders_of_Giants: On the Shoulders of a Giant
strings.CLL_Shoulders_of_Giants_desc:
To understand the reasons why Colombia burns, one must look to three souls whose legacy is the violence that now unfolds.

While fascists and self-serving despots may seek to proselytize elsewise, of them only one truly cared for the people when he served as president. Only one of them sought to uphold their rights, indifferent of who they were or from what land they came. Only one looked into their eyes and spoke as their equal, not their overlord. Only one died a martyr.

It is his name they chant in the streets of the East and whisper behind close doors everywhere across the land. It is his banner they fly and his dream they uphold in Tunja.

For in his own words, “If I die, avenge me.”
strings.CLL_Far_From_Any_Road_desc:
Deep in the hushing plains, the revolutionaries dwell, fighting not only the region's hot and humid climate, but also the threat of time. Deprived of any substantial resources, the insurmountable orient does not offer the best conditions for carrying out the revolution.

The “Wild East” as it can be called should not be mistaken for an idyllically pastroal land however, and any outsiders who folly venturing towards its green heart will meet an almost certain demise.
strings.CLL_Burning_Plains_desc:
The Eastern Plains possess but two great treasures: their natural beauty and the riches buried beneath their soil. In the grim reality forced upon the revolutionaries, they have forsaken the former to exploit the latter, turning once unspoiled landscapes into scarred mining pits and endless fields of cash crops.

The rivers run thinner, the serranías grow barren, and with the specter of war darkening the horizon, many wonder whether this fragile system will withstand the toll of a looming conflict against a far mightier enemy—or if the East will finally wither into desolation, and become a shadow of its former vitality.
strings.CLL_Red_Rose_Army_desc:
The Revolutionary Defense Corps of Colombia stand not as brothers forged by shared ideals, but as comrades bound by the scars of their common suffering. From Navas Pardo's elite Lanceros to Yosa's ferocious Raiders, every faction has glimpsed the cruel face of the Old Republic, a face that has ground them beneath its heel.

Their thirst for change, born of agony, fuels their relentless march toward revolution. Yet, even as they battle a treacherous shortage of resources and weather the storms of internal strife, their hunger for justice drives them ever forward, ready to reshape the fate of a broken nation.
strings.CLL_Revolutionary_Coalition_desc:
Despite the historical American animosity against leftism, the Colombian Revolutionary Union benefits from the backing of a Pan-American coalition of nations, led by the United States.

The Pro-Democracy and Pro-American ideology of the Gaitanistas, alongside the despotism of the fascist proxies that battle for the country have ensured the Front is democracy's best chance at retaking the Athens of South America.
For now, the OFN, Mexico, Cuba and Venezuela have provided plenty of support to the movement, and should they continue to do so, the Front may be able to achieve victory when the howling of cannons haunts Colombia again.
strings.CLL_Revolutionary_Coalition_1_desc:
A grave blow was struck against the Front when the United States ceased its aid programs, which provided the Front with the bulk of its military and civilian needs. With the state still dependent on foreign aid, its rapid shift towards the Veracruz Pact, of whom all remaining backers participate in, should not come as a surprise.

While the Pact may be strong in its will, it cannot be doubted that their aid will pale in comparison to what Uncle Sam could have provided and one can only hope that the revolutionarys' enduring fervor will be enough to carry them to victory.
strings.CLL_Revolutionary_Coalition_2_desc: The once mighty coalition which supplied the Front has perished by the hand of personal interest. Venezuela is the last nation to which the weakened front clings.
strings.CLL_Jewel_of_the_East_desc:
The crowning achievement of the Revolutionary Army during the Civil War was the capture of Tunja, a city whose political allegiance had been traded many times in the country's history. Tunja, or The Pearl of the East as it has come to be known, stands as the FR's largest stronghold and the only city from which a war can be waged.

Its population has massively swelled in the years since the truce as hundreds flee the oppressive governments in the west and its industry has almost doubled. Though the Front is still undeniably dependent on imports for its survival, it is clear that without the city, the entire war effort would collapse.
strings.CLL_Jewel_tt: Not holding Tunja or any other major city for a prolonged period of time will result in the collapse of our war effort.

strings.CLL_guerilla_training_desc: Due to the vast topological and environmental diversity of Colombia, our troops must be prepared to move through the most difficult terrains in the world, ranging from the Amazonian jungle to the Andes. With OFN advisors training our men in the latest tactics in asymmetrical warfare, we can move quicker from our positions in eastern Colombia while minimizing logistic difficulties.
